If the first and the \((2n-1)^{th}\) term of an A.P, a G.P. and a H.P. are equal and their \(n^{th}\) terms are \(a,b\) and \(c\) respectively then
questions.sol: The \(n\)th term is the middle term, so \(a,b,c\) are the A.M., G.M. and H.M. of the two equal end terms \(p,q\): \(a\ge b\ge c\) and \(ac=\dfrac{p+q}2\cdot\dfrac{2pq}{p+q}=pq=b^2\); when \(p=q\) all three coincide, \(a=b=c\).

questions.q: For \(0<\phi<\dfrac\pi2\), if \(x=\sum\limits_{n=0}^\infty\cos^{2n}\phi\), \(y=\sum\limits_{n=0}^\infty\sin^{2n}\phi\) and \(z=\sum\limits_{n=0}^\infty\cos^{2n}\phi\sin^{2n}\phi\), then
questions.sol: \(x=\dfrac1{\sin^2\phi}\), \(y=\dfrac1{\cos^2\phi}\), \(z=\dfrac1{1-\sin^2\phi\cos^2\phi}\). So \(\dfrac1z=1-\dfrac1{xy}\), i.e. \(xyz=xy+z\); and \(x+y=xy\), so also \(xyz=x+y+z\). (The book key prints only (b).)

Let \(a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots\) be an arithmetic progression with \(a_1=7\) and common difference \(8\). Let \(T_1,T_2,T_3,\ldots\) be such that \(T_1=3\) and \(T_{n+1}-T_n=a_n\) for \(n\ge1\). Then, which of the following is/are true?

(i) The value of \(x+y+z\) is \(15\). If \(a,x,y,z,b\) are in A.P. while the value of \(\dfrac1x+\dfrac1y+\dfrac1z\) is \(\dfrac53\). If \(a,x,y,z,b\) are in H.P. then find \(a\) and \(b\).
(ii) If \(x,y,z\) are in H.P. then show that \(\log(x+z)+\log(x+z-2y)=2\log(x-z)\).
questions.sol:
(i) A.P.: \(x+y+z=\frac32(a+b)=15\), so \(a+b=10\). H.P.: \(\frac1x+\frac1y+\frac1z=\frac32\left(\frac1a+\frac1b\right)=\frac53\), so \(\frac{a+b}{ab}=\frac{10}9\), \(ab=9\).
(ii) \(y=\dfrac{2xz}{x+z}\) gives \((x+z)(x+z-2y)=(x+z)^2-4xz=(x-z)^2\); take logarithms.

questions.q: If the \(m^{th}\), \(n^{th}\) and \(p^{th}\) terms of an A.P and G.P. are equal and are \(x,y,z\) then prove that \(x^{y-z}\cdot y^{z-x}\cdot z^{x-y}=1\).
The interior angles of a polygon are in A.P. The smallest angle is \(120^\circ\) and the common difference is \(5^\circ\). Find the number of sides of the polygon.
Let the angles of a triangle \(ABC\) be in A.P. and let \(b:c=\sqrt3:\sqrt2\). Find the angle \(A\).

If \(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n\) are in A.P. where \(a_i>0\) for all \(i\), show that \(\dfrac1{\sqrt{a_1}+\sqrt{a_2}}+\dfrac1{\sqrt{a_2}+\sqrt{a_3}}+\ldots+\dfrac1{\sqrt{a_{n-1}}+\sqrt{a_n}}=\dfrac{n-1}{\sqrt{a_1}+\sqrt{a_n}}\)
questions.sol: Rationalising, each term is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{a_{k+1}}-\sqrt{a_k}}d\). The sum telescopes to \(\dfrac{\sqrt{a_n}-\sqrt{a_1}}d=\dfrac{a_n-a_1}{d(\sqrt{a_n}+\sqrt{a_1})}=\dfrac{n-1}{\sqrt{a_1}+\sqrt{a_n}}\).

questions.q: Does there exist a G.P. containing \(27\), \(8\) and \(12\) as three of its terms? If it exists, how many such progressions are possible?
questions.sol: \(8,12,18,27\) is a G.P. with ratio \(\frac32\). Inserting further means (ratio \(\left(\frac32\right)^{1/k}\), \(k=1,2,3,\ldots\)) gives infinitely many such progressions.

questions.q: Find three numbers \(a,b,c\) between \(2\) and \(18\) such that (i) their sum is \(25\) (ii) \(2,a,b\) are consecutive terms of an A.P. (iii) the numbers \(b,c,18\) are consecutive terms of a G.P.

If \(n\) is a natural number such that \(n=p_1^{\alpha_1}\cdot p_2^{\alpha_2}\cdot p_3^{\alpha_3}\ldots p_k^{\alpha_k}\) and \(p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_k\) are distinct primes, then show that \(\log n\ge k\log2\).
questions.sol: Each \(p_i\ge2\) and each \(\alpha_i\ge1\), so \(n\ge2\cdot2\cdots2=2^k\); take logarithms.

questions.q: The sum of the squares of three distinct real numbers, which are in G.P. is \(s^2\). If their sum is \(\alpha s\), show that \(\alpha^2\in\left(\dfrac13,1\right)\cup(1,3)\)
questions.sol: Numbers \(\frac ar,a,ar\): \(\alpha^2=\dfrac{\left(r+\frac1r+1\right)^2}{r^2+\frac1{r^2}+1}=\dfrac{(t+1)^2}{t^2-1}=\dfrac{t+1}{t-1}\) with \(t=r+\frac1r\). Distinct real numbers need \(|t|>2\): for \(t>2\), \(\alpha^2\in(1,3)\); for \(t<-2\), \(\alpha^2\in\left(\frac13,1\right)\).

questions.q: If \(\log_32\), \(\log_3(2^x-5)\) and \(\log_3\left(2^x-\dfrac72\right)\) are in arithmetic progression, determine the value of \(x\).

Let \(p\) be the first of the \(n\) arithmetic means between two numbers and \(q\) the first of \(n\) harmonic means between the same numbers. Show that \(q\) does not lie between \(p\) and \(\left(\dfrac{n+1}{n-1}\right)^2p\)
questions.sol: For numbers \(a,b\): \(p=\dfrac{na+b}{n+1}\), \(q=\dfrac{(n+1)ab}{a+nb}\). Eliminating \(b=(n+1)p-na\): \(na^2-[(n+1)p+(n-1)q]a+npq=0\). As \(a\) is real, the discriminant is \(\ge0\): \((n-1)^2q^2-2(n^2+1)pq+(n+1)^2p^2\ge0\), i.e. \((q-p)\left(q-\left(\frac{n+1}{n-1}\right)^2p\right)\ge0\). So \(q\) cannot lie between the two values.

questions.q: If \(S_1,S_2,S_3,\ldots,S_n\) are the sums of infinite geometric series whose first terms are \(1,2,3,\ldots,n\) and whose common ratios are \(\dfrac12,\dfrac13,\dfrac14,\ldots,\dfrac1{n+1}\) respectively, then find the values of \(S_1^2+S_2^2+S_3^2+\ldots+S_{2n-1}^2\).
The real number \(x_1,x_2,x_3\) satisfying the equation \(x^3-x^2+\beta x+\gamma=0\) are in A.P. Find the intervals in which \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\) lie.

The fourth power of the common difference of an arithmetic progression with integer entries is added to the product of any four consecutive terms of it, prove that the resulting sum is square of an integer.

Let \(a_1,a_2,\ldots\) be positive real number in G.P. for each \(n\), let \(A_n,G_n,H_n\) be respectively, the arithmetic mean, geometric mean, harmonic mean of \(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n\). Find an expression for the geometric mean of \(G_1,G_2,\ldots,G_n\) in terms of \(A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_n\), \(H_1,H_2,\ldots,H_n\).
questions.sol: For the G.P. \(a,ar,\ldots,ar^{n-1}\): \(A_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{n(r-1)}\), \(H_n=\dfrac{nar^{n-1}(r-1)}{r^n-1}\), so \(A_nH_n=a^2r^{n-1}=G_n^2\). Hence \(G_k=\sqrt{A_kH_k}\) and \((G_1G_2\cdots G_n)^{1/n}=(A_1\cdots A_nH_1\cdots H_n)^{1/2n}\).

questions.q: Let \(a\) and \(b\) are positive real numbers. If \(a,A_1,A_2,b\) are in arithmetic progression \(a,G_1,G_2,b\) are in G.P. and \(a,H_1,H_2,b\) are in H.P. show that \(\dfrac{G_1G_2}{H_1H_2}=\dfrac{A_1+A_2}{H_1+H_2}=\dfrac{(2a+b)(a+2b)}{9ab}\)
If \(a,b\) and \(c\) are in arithmetic progression and \(a^2,b^2\) and \(c^2\) are in harmonic progression, then prove that either \(a=b=c\) or \(a,b\) and \(-c/2\) are in geometric progression
questions.sol: \(2b=a+c\) and \(b^2(a^2+c^2)=2a^2c^2\). With \(a^2+c^2=4b^2-2ac\): \(2b^4-acb^2-a^2c^2=0\), i.e. \((b^2-ac)(2b^2+ac)=0\). \(b^2=ac\) with \(2b=a+c\) gives \(a=b=c\); otherwise \(b^2=a\cdot\left(-\frac c2\right)\).

questions.q: If \(a,b,c\) are positive numbers, then prove that \((1+a)^7(1+b)^7(1+c)^7>7^7a^4b^4c^4\)
questions.sol: \((1+a)(1+b)(1+c)>a+b+c+ab+bc+ca+abc\ge7\left(a^4b^4c^4\right)^{1/7}\) by AM–GM on the \(7\) terms. Raise to the power \(7\).

questions.q: If total number of runs scored in \(n\) matches is \(\left(\dfrac{n+1}4\right)(2^{n+1}-n-2)\) where \(n>1\), and the runs scored in the \(k^{th}\) match are given by \(k\cdot2^{n+1-k}\), where \(1\le k\le n\). Find \(n\).

If \(a_n=\dfrac34-\left(\dfrac34\right)^2+\left(\dfrac34\right)^3+\ldots+(-1)^{n-1}\left(\dfrac34\right)^n\) and \(b_n=1-a_n\), then find the least natural number \(n_0\) such that \(b_n>a_n\ \forall\ n\ge n_0\).
questions.sol: \(a_n=\frac37\left[1-\left(-\frac34\right)^n\right]\). \(b_n>a_n\) means \(a_n<\frac12\), i.e. \(\left(-\frac34\right)^n>-\frac16\). True for even \(n\); for odd \(n\) it needs \(\left(\frac34\right)^n<\frac16\), i.e. \(n\ge7\). It fails at \(n=5\), so \(n_0=6\).

questions.q: If three complex numbers are in A.P., then they lie on a circle in the complex plane.
questions.sol: In an A.P. the middle number is the mid-point of the other two, so the three points are collinear.

In a triangle \(ABC\) if \(\cot A,\cot B,\cot C\) are in A.P., then \(a^2,b^2,c^2\) are in .............. progression.
questions.sol: \(\cot A=\dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{4\Delta}\) etc. \(2\cot B=\cot A+\cot C\) gives \(2(c^2+a^2-b^2)=2b^2\), i.e. \(2b^2=a^2+c^2\).

questions.q: The sides of a triangle inscribed in a given circle subtend angles \(\alpha,\beta\) and \(\gamma\) at the centre. The minimum value of the arithmetic mean of \(\cos\left(\alpha+\dfrac\pi2\right)\), \(\cos\left(\beta+\dfrac\pi2\right)\) and \(\cos\left(\gamma+\dfrac\pi2\right)\) is equal to ..............
questions.sol: The mean is \(-\dfrac{\sin\alpha+\sin\beta+\sin\gamma}3\) with \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=2\pi\). The sum of sines is greatest when \(\alpha=\beta=\gamma=\frac{2\pi}3\): \(\frac{3\sqrt3}2\).

questions.q: The sum of the first \(n\) terms of the series \(1^2+2\cdot2^2+3^2+2\cdot4^2+5^2+2\cdot6^2+\ldots\) is \(\dfrac{n(n+1)^2}2\), when \(n\) is even. When \(n\) is odd, the sum is ............
Let the harmonic mean and geometric mean of two positive numbers be in the ratio \(4:5\). Then the two numbers are in the ratio ..........
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{2\sqrt{ab}}{a+b}=\dfrac45\) gives \(\sqrt{\frac ab}+\sqrt{\frac ba}=\frac52\), so \(\sqrt{\frac ab}=2\) or \(\frac12\).

questions.q: Let \(p\) and \(q\) be roots of the equation \(x^2-2x+A=0\) and let \(r\) and \(s\) be the roots of the equation \(x^2-18x+B=0\). If \(p<q<r<s\) are in arithmetic progression, then \(A=\) .... and \(B=\) ............
Let \(x\) be the arithmetic mean and \(y,z\) be the two geometric means between any two positive numbers. Then \(\dfrac{y^3+z^3}{xyz}=\) ........

Column IColumn II
(A) The minimum value of \(\dfrac{x^2+2x+4}{x+2}\) is(p) \(0\)
(B) Let \(A\) and \(B\) be \(3\times3\) matrices of real numbers, where \(A\) is symmetric, \(B\) is skew-symmetric, and \((A+B)(A-B)=(A-B)(A+B)\). If \((AB)^t=(-1)^kAB\), where \((AB)^t\) is the transpose of the matrix \(AB\), then the possible values of \(k\) are(q) \(1\)
(C) Let \(a=\log_3\log_32\). An integer \(k\) satisfying \(1<2^{(-k+3^{-a})}<2\), must be less than(r) \(2\)
(D) If \(\sin\theta=\cos\varphi\), then the possible values of \(\dfrac1\pi\left(\theta\pm\varphi-\dfrac\pi2\right)\) are(s) \(3\)
questions.sol: (A) \((x+2)+\dfrac4{x+2}-2\ge2\) for \(x>-2\): (r). (B) The condition gives \(AB=BA\); \((AB)^t=B^tA^t=-BA=-AB\), so \(k\) is odd: (q), (s). (C) \(3^{-a}=\log_23\), so \(0<\log_23-k<1\) gives \(k=1\), which is less than \(2\) and \(3\): (r), (s). (D) \(\cos\left(\frac\pi2-\theta\right)=\cos\varphi\) gives \(\theta\pm\varphi-\frac\pi2=-2n\pi\), an even multiple of \(\pi\): (p), (r).

\(T_r\) is always a/an
questions.sol: \(V_{r+1}-V_r=3r^2+2r+1\), so \(T_r=3r^2+2r-1=(3r-1)(r+1)\), a product of two integers greater than \(1\).

Let \(V_r\) denote the sum of \(1^{st}\) \(r\) terms of an arithmetic progression (A.P.) whose \(1^{st}\) term is \(r\) and the common difference is \(2r-1\). Let \(T_r=V_{r+1}-V_r-2\) and \(Q_r=T_{r+1}-T_r\) for \(r=1,2,\ldots\)
Which of the following is a correct statement?
opts: \(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3,\ldots\) are in A.P. with common difference \(5\).
\(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3,\ldots\) are in A.P. with common difference \(6\).
\(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3,\ldots\) are in A.P. with common difference \(11\).
questions.sol: \(T_r=3r^2+2r-1\), so \(Q_r=T_{r+1}-T_r=6r+5\): an A.P. with common difference \(6\).

Let \(A_1,G_1\) and \(H_1\) denote the arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means respectively of two distinct positive numbers. For \(n\ge2\) let \(A_{n-1}\) and \(H_{n-1}\) have arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means as \(A_n,G_n,H_n\) respectively.
Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.sol: \(G_n^2=A_{n-1}H_{n-1}\) and for two numbers \(A\cdot H=G^2\), so \(A_nH_n=G_n^2=A_{n-1}H_{n-1}\). Thus \(A_nH_n\) is constant and all \(G_n\) are equal.

questions.q:
Comprehension
Let \(A_1,G_1\) and \(H_1\) denote the arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means respectively of two distinct positive numbers. For \(n\ge2\) let \(A_{n-1}\) and \(H_{n-1}\) have arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means as \(A_n,G_n,H_n\) respectively.
Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.sol: \(A_n\) is the mean of \(A_{n-1}\) and the smaller number \(H_{n-1}\), so \(A_n<A_{n-1}\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
Let \(A_1,G_1\) and \(H_1\) denote the arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means respectively of two distinct positive numbers. For \(n\ge2\) let \(A_{n-1}\) and \(H_{n-1}\) have arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means as \(A_n,G_n,H_n\) respectively.
Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.sol: \(A_nH_n\) is constant and \(A_n\) decreases, so \(H_n\) increases.

Statement - 2 : The numbers \(b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4\) are in H.P.
opts: Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is a correct explanation of Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is NOT a correct explanation for Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is False
Statement-1 is False, Statement-2 is True.
questions.sol: \(b\)'s are \(a,\ a(1+r),\ a(1+r+r^2),\ a(1+r+r^2+r^3)\) with \(r\ne1\). Differences \(ar,ar^2,ar^3\) are unequal (not A.P.); ratios are unequal (not G.P.); e.g. \(1,3,7,15\) is not in H.P. either.

Let \(X\) be the set consisting of the first \(2018\) terms of the arithmetic progression \(1,6,11,\ldots\), and \(Y\) be the set consisting of the first \(2018\) terms of the arithmetic progression \(9,16,23,\ldots\) Then, the number of elements in the set \(X\cup Y\) is _____.
questions.sol: Common terms: \(16,51,86,\ldots\) (difference \(35\)), up to the last term of \(X\), \(10086\): \(16+35k\le10086\) gives \(288\) terms. \(|X\cup Y|=2018+2018-288\).

questions.q: Let \(AP(a;d)\) denote the set of all the terms of an infinite arithmetic progression with first term \(a\) and common difference \(d>0\). If \(AP(1;3)\cap AP(2;5)\cap AP(3;7)=AP(a;d)\), then \(a+d\) equals _____.
questions.sol: The first common term is \(52\) (\(52=1+3\cdot17=2+5\cdot10=3+7\cdot7\)) and the common difference is \(\text{lcm}(3,5,7)=105\). \(a+d=157\).
